notes:
Circuit: single-loop ladder. Current source I-DC 100mA (left, x~130) drives a top rail y~357 that runs left-to-right through R0=50ohm and R1=100ohm to V-DC 1V (right, x~705). Shunt branches: C3=1.5F at x~286 from top rail to bottom rail; a series C2 (unlabelled, plates at y~393/411, x~486) + L6=0.75mH at x~490 from the mid-rail node down to the bottom rail. Bottom rail y~630 runs the full width and carries the GND symbol at (412,667).

NET MAP (5 nets):
  0  = ground rail y~630 from x~133 to x~711: I-DC bottom (5.1), C3 bottom (3.0), L6 bottom (6.1), V-DC bottom (4.1), GND (7.0).
  n1 = top rail left segment y~357, x~136..323: I-DC top (5.0), C3 top lead (3.1) via the x~288 drop, left end of R0 (0.0).
  n2 = top rail middle segment x~450..523 including the T at (490,356): right end of R0 (0.1), left end of R1 (1.0), top plate lead of C2 (2.1).
  n3 = top rail right segment x~651..705 plus the corner down to the source: right end of R1 (1.1), V-DC top (4.0). Verified with edges.py: e5 (651,363)->(703,360) and e7 (705,438)->(705,363) meet at corner site S2, so this is one net.
  n4 = short vertical between the bottom plate of C2 (2.0, port at (484,450)) and the top of L6 (6.0, port at (481,480)). Two terminals only, which is correct: C2 and L6 are in series in that shunt leg.

SITE DECISIONS (all four CRITICAL sites + S1 read at 5x/6x zoom):
  S0 (490,356) deg3 -> JUNCTION. Clean T: the vertical drop to C2's top plate ends on the horizontal top rail; no hop, no jog, and the rail is continuous through it. A 'crossing' reading is impossible here - the vertical branch simply terminates, there is no fourth branch to pass through to, and it would strand C2+L6 on a one-terminal net with no return path.
  S1 (289,360) deg3 -> JUNCTION (not flagged CRITICAL, recorded anyway). Same clean T where the drop to C3's top plate meets the top rail. Reading it as anything else would leave C3 with a dangling top terminal.
  S19 (483,629) deg3 -> JUNCTION. T where the inductor's bottom lead lands on the bottom rail. Crossing is impossible: the bottom rail is the only return path for the C2/L6 leg.
  S20 (413,631) deg4 -> JUNCTION. The GND symbol's stem rises to the bottom rail here. Tracer reports deg4 because the GND stem stub is split either side of the rail, but visually it is a T from below. GND must be on the rail, so junction; any other reading would put the GND symbol on its own isolated net and violate the 'GND is net 0' rule.
  S21 (286,636) deg3 -> JUNCTION. T where C3's bottom lead lands on the bottom rail. Crossing would strand C3's lower terminal.
  No site on this sheet shows a solder dot or a hop/jog; the drafter used plain Ts throughout and there is not a single true four-way wire crossing in the drawing. The remaining sites (S5, S6, S7, S9, S10, S12, S13, S14, S16, S17) are all the value labels ('50ohm', '100ohm', '1.5F', '1V', '0.75mH', '100mA') brushing a wire or a symbol outline; none of them are wire-to-wire and all were left at the tracer default (they do not change the netlist).

PORT FIXES:
  #3 Capacitor (1.5F): the tracer had t1 pointing at p2@(326,484), which is ink from the '1.5F' text, not a lead - that produced the single-terminal net n5. Repointed t1 to p1@(287,421), the real top lead that runs up to the top rail at S1. t0 stays p0@(284,494), the bottom lead.
  #4 V-DC (1V): BOTH terminals were on text. t0 was p2@(651,537), which is the 'H' of the neighbouring '0.75mH' label, and t1 was p3@(754,503), the '1' of the '1V' label; that produced single-terminal nets n6 and n7. Repointed t0 to p1@(705,438) (top lead, the '+' side, running up to the top rail) and t1 to p0@(707,538) (bottom lead, running down to the ground rail). V-DC is a 2-terminal part so terminal order is not scored, but top->bottom matches the drawn +/- anyway.
  Confirmed correct and left alone: R0 (p1 left = t0, p0 right = t1), R1 (p2 left = t0, p0 right = t1), C2 (p0 top = t1, p1 bottom = t0), I-DC (p0 top = t0, p1 bottom = t1), L6 (p1 top = t0, p0 bottom = t1), GND (p0 = t0). The extra 'unused port' warnings on R0, R1, I-DC and L6 are all label ink touching the bounding box, not leads.

CLASSES: all eight symbols match their labels - resistor zig-zags, two parallel-plate capacitors, a coil inductor, a circle-with-arrow current source, a circle-with-+/- voltage source, and a three-bar ground. No re-classification needed. The middle capacitor C2 carries no printed value on the sheet; that is a drafting omission, not a class error, and it does not affect the netlist.

UNRESOLVED: nothing. All 8 components have every terminal on a net, 5 nets, ERC clean, no net with fewer than 2 terminals.
